title: MemoryStand — presenter cut
presenterDisclosure: Presenter synthesised from the author's own photograph.
_notes: MEASURED CONSTRAINTS of grok image_to_video, established before building on them:
- a clip is ~6.04s at 24fps, 496x608 PORTRAIT. Duration is not controllable, so the
script is written in SHOTS of <=20 spoken words rather than 15s beats.
- it generates AUDIO as well as video, and if you do not give it words IT INVENTS THEM.
An early test with a motion-only prompt came back saying 'So, to summarize the key
findings from our analysis, we can conclude that the results are promising' -- generic
filler nobody wrote. Shipping that would put invented words in the author's mouth, in a
project whose entire argument is that unverified claims must be labelled.
- given the exact line it reproduces it verbatim. So every shot passes its line, and
make_clips.py TRANSCRIBES each generated clip and fails the shot if it drifts.
shots 5a/5b -> live /decide response, quoted verbatim in README

lines: Mem0 — an LLM picks ADD/UPDATE/DELETE. No confidence score at all.
Zep — an LLM sets validity windows. "Model-inferred, not authoritative."
AWS AgentCore — extraction and consolidation are LLM prompts. No verification API.
panelData.footnote: Each line cites the vendor's own docs or issue tracker. See README.

shots: Every shipping agent-memory system asks a model whether its own memory is true. Mem0, Zep, AWS AgentCore.
MemoryStand asks CloudWatch instead — and refuses the promotion when CloudWatch disagrees.

panelData.headline: Nobody lied. The memory is still false.
panelData.body: And it will be handed to an agent at the next incident. That is how a memory store fills with true-sounding operational folklore.

shots: It's an engineer at two in the morning who restarts a service, watches the page clear, and reports in good faith that the restart fixed it —

panelData.footnote: benchmarks/poisoning.md · judge arm run live, not estimated

shots: So we measured it. Six hundred poisoned claims, plus honest ones as a control. Trusting the caller admits every attack.
An LLM judge blocks every attack — and every honest claim too.

panelData.label: model calls on the promotion path
panelData.body: backend/trust.py imports no model client, and a runtime guard fails if one becomes reachable even one import away.

shots: A defence that refuses all evidence stops all poisoning, and is useless.
Only the outcome gate tells the two apart —
and it does it with zero model calls on the promotion path.
Here it is deciding. Two candidate memories: the nearer one is unconfirmed, the further one was checked against CloudWatch.
Proximity said one thing. Trust said another. Trust won.

lines: Doyle, JTMS, 1979 — a belief holds only while its justification does
CHEF, 1986 — cases retained by whether the plan actually worked

shots: None of this is a new idea. Doyle's truth maintenance systems retracted beliefs in 1979.
What's unusual is a 2026 memory system that won't let a model grade its own memory — and enforces it.
